free_cash_flow_yield: Bank cash flow statements do not describe distributable owner cash like industrial FCF.
return_on_invested_capital: Debt is an operating input for banks.
net_debt_to_ebitda: Deposits and borrowings are operating funding.
ev_to_ebitda: Enterprise value is economically misleading for banks.
altman_z: Industrial bankruptcy model is not calibrated for banks.
sales_multiple: Interest and fee income is not comparable to industrial sales.
ev_to_ebit: Enterprise value is economically misleading for banks.
ev_to_fcf: Industrial FCF is not comparable for banks.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Receivable days do not represent bank credit quality.
days_sales_outstanding: Receivable days do not represent bank credit quality.
incremental_margin: Efficiency ratio is the bank operating-leverage measure.
capex_to_depreciation: Physical reinvestment is not the bank value-creation engine.
piotroski_f: Generic accounting checklist omits credit and capital quality.

current_ratio: Insurer liquidity and solvency require statutory measures.
peg: Universal PEG does not normalize underwriting cycles or reserve development.
free_cash_flow_yield: Industrial FCF is distorted by premiums, claims, reserves and investment flows.
return_on_invested_capital: Insurer leverage and float make generic ROIC misleading.
cash_conversion: Claims reserves break industrial earnings-to-cash comparisons.
net_debt_to_ebitda: EBITDA leverage is not an insurer solvency measure.
ev_to_ebitda: EV/EBITDA is not an insurer-standard valuation measure.
ev_to_fcf: Industrial FCF is not comparable for insurers.
altman_z: Industrial bankruptcy model is not calibrated for insurers.
piotroski_f: Generic accounting checklist omits underwriting and reserve quality.
capex_to_depreciation: Physical reinvestment is not the insurer value-creation engine.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Receivable days do not represent insurer underwriting quality.
sales_multiple: Premium revenue is not comparable to industrial sales, and EV is not an insurer measure.
ev_to_ebit: Enterprise value is economically misleading for insurers, on the same grounds as EV/EBITDA.
gross_profits_to_assets: Insurers report no gross-profit line; premiums less claims is underwriting income.
incremental_margin: Incremental margin over an underwriting and reserve-development cycle is noise, not operating leverage.
days_sales_outstanding: Premium receivable days do not represent insurer underwriting quality.

combined_ratio: Combined ratio applies to P&C underwriting, not life products.

peg: EPS is distorted by property depreciation.
forward_pe: P/FFO is the standard earnings multiple for REITs.
free_cash_flow_yield: AFFO better reflects recurring property cash generation.
return_on_invested_capital: Generic ROIC is distorted by property accounting.
current_ratio: REIT liquidity is better assessed through debt maturity and coverage.
altman_z: Industrial bankruptcy model is not calibrated for REITs.

free_cash_flow_yield: Regulated utilities commonly fund large mandated capital programs.

peg: Point estimates are dominated by commodity-cycle assumptions.
operating_margin_trend: Trailing margin trend for a producer is the realized commodity price, not structural improvement.
incremental_margin: Incremental margin against a commodity-driven revenue denominator is cycle contamination; NEM published 128.2%.
fcf_growth_3y: Three-year FCF growth for a producer tracks the commodity cycle, not capital discipline.
gross_profits_to_assets: Gross profitability moves with realized price rather than asset productivity.

altman_z: Industrial distress scores do not represent pipeline and binary-event risk.

price_to_book: Book value does not capture pipeline probability.
free_cash_flow_yield: Cash burn should be evaluated as runway.
altman_z: Industrial distress scores do not represent clinical-stage solvency or binary-event risk.
return_on_invested_capital: Pre-profit biotechnology has no stable operating-return denominator.

capex_to_depreciation: A low capex-to-depreciation ratio is structural for a fabless designer that outsources fabrication, not evidence of under-investment. Distinguishing fabless from integrated manufacturers requires a filing parse this pipeline does not yet do, so the interpretation is suppressed for the whole industry rather than applied wrongly to part of it.
inventory_days_trend: Semiconductor inventory swings with the industry cycle and customer build plans; a rising trend is not an accounting-quality signal.

price_to_book: Insurance brokers earn commission and fee income and take no underwriting risk or investment float; acquisition-driven goodwill in this roll-up-heavy sub-industry makes book value uninformative -- valued like an asset-light services business, not an underwriter.
altman_z: Distress model calibrated for asset-heavy manufacturers; a fee-based broker carries no inventory or heavy fixed assets for it to read correctly.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Commission and fee income does not generate a receivable-days signal comparable to industrial DSO.

combined_ratio: Combined ratio is a P&C underwriting construct; medical loss ratio (health-plan costs over premium revenue) is the health-insurer analog.

forward_pe: Accelerated depreciation on an asset-intensive pipeline/storage base makes P/E nearly meaningless for midstream; EV/EBITDA is the sector-standard multiple.
peg: PEG compounds the same forward-P/E distortion, on the same grounds as forward_pe above.
free_cash_flow_yield: Growth capex depresses FCF during the build phase; EV/EBITDA and distribution coverage (not yet computed by this pipeline) are the standard midstream reads, not FCF yield.
current_ratio: Midstream working capital is not the liquidity signal it is for an industrial company; leverage (net_debt_to_ebitda) and interest coverage carry that read instead.

forward_pe: Airlines are a textbook peak-earnings/trough-multiple cyclical; EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle margins is preferred to a point-in-time P/E, which reads cheapest exactly at the top of the cycle.
peg: PEG compounds the same cyclical forward-P/E distortion, on the same grounds as forward_pe above.
current_ratio: Airlines run structurally low current ratios by design -- advance ticket sales are a current liability that funds operations -- so this is not the liquidity signal it is for a typical industrial company.
Long-cycle program working capital (progress billings, customer advances) is not the short-term liquidity signal current ratio represents for a typical industrial company.
peg: Program-timing lumpiness in trailing growth breaks the PEG denominator; forward P/E against backlog-supported growth reads better.

gross_profits_to_assets: Capital-markets firms report no gross-profit line; trading and underwriting revenue over risk capital is the comparable read, approximated here by return on equity pending a computed net-revenue-per-risk-capital metric.

price_to_book: Asset managers are asset-light and fee-driven; earnings power (P/E) is the standard read, not balance-sheet book value.
net_debt_to_ebitda: Leverage is a minor input to an asset-light, fee-revenue business model.
current_ratio: Working-capital liquidity is not the balance-sheet risk that matters here; AUM, net flows, and fee-rate stability are (not yet computed by this pipeline beyond the unaudited filing-extraction layer).
gross_profits_to_assets: No meaningful gross-profit-to-assets frame for a fee-based, asset-light business.

altman_z: Heavy land and work-in-process inventory carrying, plus structurally elevated leverage through the build cycle, break the industrial-manufacturer calibration Altman's model assumes.
free_cash_flow_yield: Cash flow moves inversely to growth for a homebuilder: land and work-in-process spend consumes cash fastest exactly when order growth (and future revenue) is strongest, so FCF yield reads worst at the best points in the cycle.
ev_to_fcf: Same cash-flow-inverted-to-growth distortion as free_cash_flow_yield above.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Homebuilder receivables are not a meaningful earnings-quality signal set against work-in-process inventory accounting.
accruals_ratio: Land and work-in-process inventory accounting produces structurally large accruals unrelated to the earnings-quality signal this ratio targets elsewhere.

forward_pe: Merchant power prices are commodity-cyclical; a point-in-time P/E is the same peak-earnings/trough-multiple trap it is for other commodity producers.
peg: PEG compounds the same cyclical forward-P/E distortion, on the same grounds as forward_pe above.

_comment: Two rules per metric per business profile. APPLICABILITY: `rules` declares whether a metric is meaningful for a profile at all (suppressed/replaced/applied). REQUIRED_FOR_SCORE: `required_for_score` declares which metrics a parent factor cannot publish without. Both are read by the LIVE scorer (pipeline/scorer.py) as well as the v2 layer -- previously only the v2 shadow path consulted this file, so the correct insurer rules below existed and governed nothing a user saw. See research/audit/CURRENT_MODEL_AUDIT.md section 5.

required_for_score._comment: category -> metrics the category score cannot be published without. A missing required metric makes the parent category null rather than quietly renormalizing onto whatever else resolved. Publishing a Value score of 96 for an insurer whose price-to-book was never scored is the failure this prevents.
